instructions: Turn the broiler on high and set a rack about 6 inches below it.
Put the whole peppers on a baking sheet and broil them for 20 to 25 minutes, turning them every 6 minutes, until the skin is blackened and blistered all over.
Transfer them to a bowl, cover it with a plate and leave them for 10 minutes, until they're cool enough to handle.
Meanwhile, chop the garlic and squeeze the juice from half the lemon.
Peel the blackened skin off the peppers and pull out the stems and seeds.

Put the peppers in a food processor with the 2 tsp olive oil, garlic, 1/3 cup walnuts, 2 tbsp breadcrumbs, 4 tsp pomegranate molasses, 2 tsp tomato paste, 3/4 tsp Aleppo pepper, 1/4 tsp cumin, 1/4 tsp sumac, 1/4 tsp salt and the lemon juice.
Pulse until it's mostly smooth with a little texture left. Taste it, and add a squeeze from the other lemon half if it's flat.
Warm the pitas in the oven for 2 to 3 minutes, then cut them into wedges.
Spoon the muhammara into a shallow bowl. Serve with the warm pita.
Leftovers keep in the fridge for up to 5 days in a sealed container.
method_notes: Both read versions blacken whole red peppers, peel them and blend them with walnuts, breadcrumbs, garlic, cumin, pomegranate molasses, olive oil, lemon and chili flakes until thick and a little chunky. Tasting Table (the lead) broils the peppers and adds tomato paste, sumac and Aleppo pepper, while SBS uses paprika, a full tablespoon of cumin, more oil and molasses, and pulses the walnuts in last so they stay chunky. This follows Tasting Table's ratios scaled from 6 servings to 4, with SBS's 5 day fridge keeping time.
